summary: Babel preset ships obfuscated payload executed via downloaded Bun runtime at preinstall
details: @ornikar/babel-preset-base@6.0.7 declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs prefers a locally installed `bun` and otherwise downloads the Bun v1.3.13 runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it (execFileSync) against a sibling file math_init.js in the package directory. math_init.js is a ~727KB obfuscator.io-style string-array/shuffle-obfuscated JavaScript file (hex identifiers `_0xNNNN`, an array-rotation function shuffling a large mixed-type constant table) whose true behavior is hidden from static review. index.js is an unremarkable ~30-line Babel preset factory, and neither the preset nor its dependencies require a second JavaScript runtime or a large adjacent JS file — the install-time behavior is unrelated to the advertised Babel-preset purpose. The alternate-runtime execution path (running the payload under Bun rather than the Node process that npm invokes) evades scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. All of this fires unconditionally on `npm install` on every installer machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
